newsitem.title: USA: Humana to buy Physician Corp. for $400 million.
newsitem.headline: Humana to buy Physician Corp. for $400 million.

text.p: Health care services provider Humana Inc., in a bid to secure its place in a rapidly consolidating marketplace, said Tuesday it signed a definitive agreement to buy Physician Corp. of America for about $400 million.
Humana, based in Louisville, Ky., will pay $7 a share for Physician, which has health maintenance organisations in Florida, Texas and Puerto Rico.
Humana also will assume about $130 million of Physician Corp. debt.

Humana shares surged to a new high for the year on the news, gaining 50 cents a share to $23.75, in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange. Physician Corp. was up 37.5 cents at $6.625 on Nasdaq.
"It is a fabulous bargain," said National Securities Corp. analyst Michael LeConey.
The transaction adds another 1.1 million members to Humana, which has 4.8 million members, and gives it over $8 billion in annual premiums, the company said.
Before the deal, Humana had $6.9 billion in annual premiums and Physician had $1.3 billion.

Humana said it expected the acquisition would add between 8 cents and 10 cents a share to its earnings in 1998. In its most recent full year, Humana earned $12 million, or 7 cents a share, but those results included a one-time charge of $200 million related to restructuring.

The news comes almost three months after Sierra Health Services Inc. said it terminated a merger agreement with Physician Corp. That deal fell apart after Physician said it would take significant additional charges in the 1996 fourth quarter to cover increased liabilities at its workers' compensation unit.
